text:
Emil Heineman's season has been a mix of good hockey and one bad moment. On Oct. 31 he was ejected for a knee-on-knee collision with Edmonton's Isaac Howard, who is now out for a couple of weeks. Since then he has stepped into Calum Ritchie's spot beside Victor Eklund and Brayden Schenn and kept producing: six assists in his last ten games, no goals.

The on-ice numbers are excellent. The Islanders take about 57% of the expected goals with him out there, nearly nine points better than without him, and they've scored about 7.5 more goals than expected in his minutes, so some luck is in there too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than 86% of forwards. NHL Edge puts his speed and shot both near the top tenth of the league.

He scored 22 goals last season, so two through 16 games (on 2.8 expected) undersells him. Evolving-Hockey added that he draws more penalties than he takes. Our range has him at 12 to 24 goals over a full season. The goals should come; the discipline needs to stay.
headline: Heineman's line is working
